title: Turning the Quotient into a Whole Point Count on a Settlement of Billed Charges
content:
How the quotient obtained on a settlement of billed charges is turned into a whole point count on a card under Personal Credit Cards turns on how long the card account has been open and on how often points have already been redeemed on it.

*Where the card account has been open at least 60 whole months and at least 3 rewards redemptions have already been posted to it*, the quotient is raised to the next whole multiple of 500 points.

*Where the card account has been open at least 60 whole months and fewer than 3 rewards redemptions have been posted to it*, the quotient is raised to the next whole multiple of 100 points.

*Where the card account has been open less than 60 whole months*, the quotient is rounded half-up to a whole point.

**Worked on a hypothetical quotient.** A quotient of 13201.4 becomes 13500 points under the first convention, 13300 points under the second and 13201 points under the third. A quotient that already sits on a multiple, say 13000, is unchanged by either of the first two conventions, since raising to the next whole multiple leaves a figure already on the multiple where it stands.

**On the boundaries.** The age of the account is read as at least, so an account open exactly 60 whole months falls with the older accounts and one open 59 whole months with the younger. The redemption count separates at 3: exactly 3 redemptions already posted belongs to the first convention, and 2 to the second. An account open less than 60 whole months takes the third convention whatever its redemption count.
